articles.title: Two Women Arrested After Three-Year-Old Boy Falls from Window in Rochdale
articles.excerpt: A three-year-old boy is in critical condition after falling from a first-floor window in Spotland Tops, Rochdale. Two women, aged 19 and 20, have been arrested on suspicion of causing serious injury to a child.
articles.content_html:
BREAKING NEWS — LIVE

Live updates, newest first.

18:27, 23 August 2026

A three-year-old boy is in critical condition after falling from a first-floor window in Spotland Tops, Rochdale. Two women, aged 19 and 20, have been arrested on suspicion of causing serious injury to a child.

A three-year-old boy is currently in critical condition after falling from a first-floor window in Rochdale. Emergency services were called to Spotland Tops in the Cutgate area shortly after 4.15pm on Saturday, August 22.

The boy was taken to hospital following the incident, where he remains under medical care. An air ambulance was also deployed to the scene to assist with the emergency response.

In connection with the incident, Greater Manchester Police (GMP) have arrested two women, aged 19 and 20, on suspicion of causing serious injury to a child. The arrests took place at an address in Blackburn, Lancashire, on Sunday, August 23.

GMP stated that inquiries into the full circumstances surrounding the incident are ongoing. Further updates are expected as the investigation progresses.

articles.title: Significant police presence at Cutgate Precinct
articles.excerpt: A significant police presence has been reported at Cutgate Precinct this evening. Details are still emerging and this story will be updated.
articles.content_html:
A significant police presence has been reported at Cutgate Precinct this evening.

Multiple officers were seen in the area of the precinct outside Miami Crispy, and residents nearby have reported ongoing police activity.

The nature of the incident has not yet been confirmed, and Greater Manchester Police has not released a statement at the time of publication.

This is a developing story and will be updated as soon as verified information becomes available. If you were in the area and have information, you can contact Greater Manchester Police on 101, or 999 in an emergency.
